item.text: {"question_id":"4B.2","answer":"The 2023 record does not show consistent restraint from using state authority in ways that could entrench incumbent or allied power. Tshisekedi maintained and repeatedly extended the state of siege, including through presidential ordinances, while replacing elected provincial governors and assemblies with military administration and subjecting civilians to military courts. Amnesty reported that military authorities appointed by him harassed and jailed journalists, detained critics, and curtailed political activity; the measure was extended more than 50 times without meaningful public debate, although the supplied evidence does not establish that each extension was personally intended to preserve power. [BATCH-0012-R03-E001, BATCH-0012-R03-E002, BATCH-0012-R03-E003, BATCH-0015-E007] During the election year, authorities restricted opposition activity: they violently dispersed a May opposition march after which Tshisekedi praised the supervising police chief; blocked Katumbi's travel and opposition sit-ins; used tear gas and beatings; banned demonstrations; arrested opposition figures; searched Kalonda's and Katumbi's residences; and detained or charged opposition-linked figures, with HRW and UN/diplomatic sources raising concerns about politically motivated intimidation. [BATCH-0002-E011, BATCH-0003-E001, BATCH-0003-E002, BATCH-0003-E003, BATCH-0003-E005, BATCH-0003-E006, BATCH-0003-E007] Authorities also prohibited a post-election opposition march amid fraud allegations, while CFR reported that protest-based challenges were expected to be forcefully suppressed and that the judiciary was compromised. [BATCH-0021-E009, BATCH-0019-E014] Electoral entrenchment concerns include ruling-coalition abuse of administrative resources, perceived CENI proximity to the government, alleged politicization surrounding CENI leadership, opaque voter-register auditing, and irregularities that damaged institutional credibility; these findings primarily concern government, CENI, or coalition actors rather than proving Tshisekedi personally directed each act. [BATCH-0001-E014, BATCH-0010-E020, BATCH-0013-E009] An aligned governor declared Tshisekedi the province's only candidate and excluded rivals rhetorically, but the evidence does not show presidential authorization, endorsement, or remedy. [BATCH-0006-E004] Countervailing evidence shows Tshisekedi instructed institutions to protect electoral materials, punish fraud, violence, exclusion, and discrimination, and support a credible process; CENI proposed a mixed external audit with conflict-of-interest safeguards, and the Constitutional Court validated 26 candidacies and reinstated two previously excluded candidates. These institutional actions are favorable but do not establish effective implementation, presidential control of CENI or the Court, or consistent non-entrenchment. [BATCH-0009-E001, BATCH-0027-E011, BATCH-0005-E005] Wartime support for armed groups, private military personnel, and expanded coercive capacity further complicates the record, but the supplied evidence does not establish that these measures were adopted specifically to preserve personal or party power. [BATCH-0011-E019, BATCH-0028-E016] Overall, the evidence supports a finding of material ruler-attributable or government-level obstruction and institutional concentration inconsistent with consistent non-entrenchment, while personal intent, responsibility for many local actions, legality, parliamentary involvement, and the security rationale remain uncertain.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0012-R03-E001","BATCH-0012-R03-E002","BATCH-0012-R03-E003","BATCH-0015-E007","BATCH-0002-E011","BATCH-0003-E001","BATCH-0003-E002","BATCH-0003-E003","BATCH-0003-E005","BATCH-0003-E006","BATCH-0003-E007","BATCH-0021-E009","BATCH-0019-E014","BATCH-0001-E014","BATCH-0010-E020","BATCH-0013-E009"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0006-E004","BATCH-0009-E001","BATCH-0027-E011","BATCH-0005-E005","BATCH-0011-E019","BATCH-0028-E016"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The evidence does not prove that Tshisekedi personally intended every emergency, electoral, police, CENI, judicial, or provincial action to entrench personal or party power.","Several adverse acts are attributed to authorities, CENI, provincial officials, security forces, or ruling-coalition actors rather than directly to the president.","The legality, parliamentary role, safeguards, and implementation of state-of-siege extensions are incompletely documented.","Some opposition arrests, searches, and security measures had stated national-security or conflict rationales; allegations of political motivation are not uniformly resolved.","The favorable directives and audit framework do not establish completion, publication, enforcement, or effective remedy."] ,"corrections_made":["Added the omitted May opposition crackdown, presidential praise for the supervising police chief, Kalonda-related arrest and searches, Diongo arrest and release, and post-election march prohibition.","Added direct qualification separating institutional authoritarian effects from proof of personal entrenchment intent.","Expanded electoral-administration evidence while preserving that CENI and coalition attribution is not equivalent to personal presidential direction.","Retained favorable institutional directives, external-audit safeguards, court reinstatement of candidates, and corrective release evidence as contrary or qualifying material."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Reopen if primary records establish Tshisekedi's personal authorization, knowledge, endorsement, or remedy regarding the provincial exclusionary statement, opposition restrictions, CENI appointments, voter-register audit, or searches and detentions.","Reopen if complete state-of-siege extension records clarify parliamentary approval, legal safeguards, duration, and whether the measure was maintained for security purposes or political entrenchment.","Reopen if final investigations or judicial outcomes resolve the alleged political motivation and accountability for security-force abuses and opposition prosecutions."]}
